A Way of Seeing... Everything

The most important thing in existence may not be what is.
It may be what can happen next.

Framing Everything asks how a universe full of possibility becomes the single reality you experience — and whether consciousness, choice, and intelligence are part of that selection.

A framework built from science, philosophy, lived experience, and one rule: when the evidence ends, the book tells you.

Book One of the My Theory of Everything series

This is a theory, not a doctrine. Reality gets the final edit.

Scientific result is not the same thing as interpretation. Analogy is not mechanism. Mystery is not evidence. When this book steps past established ground, it says so.

Why This Book

Start with the question,
not the vocabulary.

Most theories of reality begin by asking what the universe is made of. Framing Everything begins one step earlier: how does possibility become the one state that is actually lived?

That question leads through simultaneous discovery, quantum possibility, consciousness, memory, time, choice, self-organized criticality, intelligence, and finally the Loop. The claim is not that one experiment proves all of it. The claim is that these problems may be pointing at the same architecture.

Possibility is not blank. It has structure.
See the five terms ↓

The Architecture

Five Terms. One Framework.

Each one introduced, none of them exhausted.

01

The Field

The structured landscape of states reality permits: possibilities, constraints, transitions, and unequal odds. Not every imaginable thing. Not every possible thing from here.

02

The Hand

The model for how a conscious system receives, attends, acts, and participates in which reachable state becomes part of its lived history. The Hand does not override physical law.

03

The Grain

One realized state. One selected piece of the possible world becoming part of an unfolding history.

04

The Frame

The portion of a Grain integrated into one conscious experience of now. The world is larger than what any one observer can translate at once.

05

The Loop

The larger architecture: reality cycles, branches as it turns, preserves pattern, and becomes capable of noticing itself from inside the process.

Five terms. One question: what changes once the thing inside the system can notice the system?

Epistemic Discipline

The book tells you when the ground ends.

Every major claim is treated as one of three things.

Solid Ground

Documented science, history, or observation the argument can stand on.

What we know.

Contested Ground

Serious interpretations, active debates, and evidence that supports more than one explanation.

What remains open.

Off the Map

Original synthesis and speculation — clearly labeled, so possibility never gets smuggled in as proof.

What the framework is proposing.

"Maybe I am allowed to say this if enough sources let me."

Intelligence & Revision

A theory is only useful if it can survive being wrong.

The point is not to replace one rigid worldview with another. The point is to get better at noticing when the model in your head has stopped matching the world in front of you.

Intelligence is not just having a model. It is being able to revise one. Framing Everything applies that rule to the largest model we carry: what reality is, what consciousness is doing inside it, and what our choices can actually change.

  • See the assumptions hiding inside familiar explanations.
  • Separate evidence from interpretation without killing curiosity.
  • Hold a big idea strongly enough to test it and lightly enough to change it.

The Author

Christopher R. York

Christopher R. York is not asking the reader to accept a doctrine. He is asking the reader to examine a pattern with him.

A pattern thinker, producer, and founder building at the intersection of consciousness, technology, and culture. He spent two decades in marketing and artist development before turning the same systems-thinking toward the questions underneath everything.

Framing Everything is his first book. He lives and works in the southeastern United States.
